topic.subject: science
topic.title: Wastewater story
topic.scope: sewage, treatment plants, sanitation, better housekeeping, open defecation and disease

misconceptions.statement: Water that looks clear is always safe to drink.
misconceptions.why: Students equate visual clarity with purity based on everyday observation of tap water.
misconceptions.fix: Water can contain invisible dissolved impurities and harmful germs even if it appears transparent.

probe.question: If you filter muddy water until it looks clear, is it safe to drink?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, because it looks clean and has no particles.

misconceptions.statement: Diseases are caused by bad smells from open drains.
misconceptions.why: The association between foul odors and unpleasant environments leads students to assume the smell itself is the vector of illness.
misconceptions.fix: Diseases are spread by microorganisms like bacteria and viruses that breed in sewage, not by the smell itself.

probe.question: Why do people get sick near open drains?
probe.wrong_answer: Because the bad smell carries the disease into their bodies.

misconceptions.statement: Wastewater treatment plants turn sewage into pure drinking water.
misconceptions.why: Students often assume that 'treatment' implies a complete restoration to the original state of utility.
misconceptions.fix: Treatment plants clean wastewater enough to be safely released into rivers or used for irrigation, but it is not necessarily potable.

probe.question: Can we drink the water coming out of a sewage treatment plant?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, because the plant has removed all the dirt and germs.

misconceptions.statement: Chemicals are the only way to clean dirty water.
misconceptions.why: Students focus on the use of chlorine or bleach in household cleaning and ignore biological processes.
misconceptions.fix: Many treatment plants use bacteria and physical processes to break down organic waste before using chemicals.

probe.question: How do treatment plants remove organic waste from water?
probe.wrong_answer: They add strong chemicals to kill everything and dissolve the waste.
